messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — High error rate on hosted model-inference path. Autoscaler flapping observed. Root symptom: repeated container restarts with CUDA OOM and nvml resets. Paging SRE oncall. Severity: P1.

carl: saw the pager. confirming — serving runtime shows a cascade of OOMs across g4dn-pool workers, pods continually CrashLoopBackOff after scale events. Autoscaler keeps adding nodes then quickly scaling down.

lee: oncall here. what's the current customer impact?

maria: support reports 15+ customers seeing increased latency and ~5 customers getting 5xxs for requests >1s. A couple of SLA alerts triggered.

anya: attaching last error snippet from pod logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] runtime.cu: kernel launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
2026-03-15T10:12:07Z] nvml: device reset due to driver fault
```
Pod events show OOMKilled then restart, then immediate eviction during node scale-down.

carl: looks like autoscaler up -> scheduler places new shards -> heavy warmup KV/cache -> node gets memory pressure -> autoscaler thinks need more nodes but then scale down quickly because short-lived requests finish. result: thrash.

lee: can we pause autoscaler? which component? Is this cluster-autoscaler or our custom fast-scaler?

anya: it's our custom fast-scaler (autoscale-svc) — configured with short window (30s) for burst response. That short window is exactly the problem: warmup spikes look like permanent traffic.

carl: immediate mitigations: 1) disable burst autoscale for affected pool, 2) set minReplicas to current stable baseline, 3) cordon any noisy nodes to avoid further scheduling churn. I'll take 1 & 2.

lee: do it and confirm here before killing pods. Also we should block new deployments to that pool.

carl: executing now — hitting the control plane: 
```bash
# temporarily disable burst policy for g4dn-pool
redwoodctl autoscale update --pool g4dn-pool --burst-enabled false
# raise min replicas to baseline
redwoodctl autoscale update --pool g4dn-pool --min-replicas 8
```
carl: done. autoscaler accepts config, new config propagated to controller.

incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE — autoscale policy updated by carl.

anya: good. next: identify crashlooping pods and restart on fresh nodes with larger GPU memory profile. I'll patch the hotpath deployment to request more GPU memory and increase container-level memory limits to avoid OOM during KV warmup.

maria: notifying impacted customers with a short status: "We are investigating increased latencies and 5xxs; mitigation in progress. Will update within 30 minutes."

lee: advise SRE action steps: 
- disable burst autoscale (done)
- set cooldown on scale down to 10m (we should change policy)
- increase node pool base size to avoid frequent scale events
- restart crashlooping pods onto upgraded instances

anya: making a targeted patch -> will update deployment: 
```yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: runtime
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "12Gi"
            nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
          limits:
            memory: "14Gi"
```
Applying to canary first.

carl: also adding a greedy kube-scheduler predicate: prefer nodes with gpu-memory >= 24Gi for this hotpath group to avoid packing on small instances.

lee: while we patch, we should drain a couple of worst offenders to ensure they re-schedule on the new sizing. But avoid mass drains — do one at a time.

anya: listing current crashloop pods: `kubectl get pods -l app=runtime-hotpath -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running` shows 14 pods CrashLoopBackOff across 6 nodes. I'll restart pods on node-7 first.

carl: go ahead but run `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force` for the selected pods so they get scheduled on the new nodes.

anya: done for node-7 group. sample logs after restart show fewer immediate OOMs but still some warmup allocations.

deploy-bot: DEPLOY BLOCK — New deploys to runtime-hotpath blocked by carl until incident cleared.

maria: sent initial customer note. escalation asked for ETA. we'll follow up after mitigation completes.

lee: SRE action: set a temporary autoscaler cooldown config and disable scale-to-zero for the pool. carl, can you set cooldown to 10m?

carl: updating now: `redwoodctl autoscale update --pool g4dn-pool --scale-down-cooldown 600s --disable-scale-to-zero true` — applied.

incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE — scale-down-cooldown updated by carl.

anya: applying canary resource bump — monitoring metrics. Memory pressure graph shows 30% drop in OOM events on canary. Latency for warmup requests still elevated ~200-400ms.

lee: good. next risk: driver mismatch / cuda driver resets during restarts. Any kernel logs?

anya: grabbed node dmesg snippet: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.` Looks like intermittent driver resets under heavy load. We'll schedule a node image rotate to a build with newer nvidia-driver (from 535.* to 542.*).

carl: we can't rotate whole pool right now. Plan: 1) schedule progressive node upgrades while kept under minReplicas; 2) taint old nodes to avoid scheduling new pods. I'll coordinate with infra for controlled replacement.

maria: support asks for a postmortem commit to customers: include cause = autoscaler burst config + warmup memory spike + driver resets. We'll prepare a short bulletin after stabilization.

lee: assign actions: 
- carl: pause burst, raise min replicas, set cooldown, coordinate node replacement (owner)
- anya: patch resource requests, apply canary, restart CrashLoop pods in controlled batches (owner)
- maria: customer comms + status updates (owner)
- lee: permission to escalate to infra for node driver rolling (owner)

carl: assigned. starting controlled restarts across remaining nodes. doing one at a time: node-9 next.

anya: observed during restart: two pods still failed with `std::bad_alloc` at ~heap reserve step. increasing memory limit for those specific pods to 18Gi as stopgap.

carl: note — autoscale metrics show previous scale-downs were triggered by brief dip in request queue between warmup spikes. We should add a hysteresis window in autoscaler evaluation (e.g., 3m avg) to avoid reacting to short bursts. Filing a ticket: RD-INC-4307 to change default from 30s to 3m for burst window.

lee: good. include actionable rollback if new autoscaler code causes regressions. For now, we have manual mitigations live.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation in progress, customer impact decreasing. Patching resources, controlling autoscale, progressive node repair underway.

maria: customers updated: "We've applied infrastructure mitigations and are observing improving stability. We will follow up with technical details and timeline for a full fix."

anya: after all controlled restarts and canary bump, OOM events dropped to near zero. CrashLoopBackOff count reduced from 14 to 2. Latency trending down to baseline over the next 12 minutes.

lee: ok — continuing monitoring. carl, please do handoff in 20 minutes to next oncall and summarize actions in postmortem skeleton.

carl: will do. summary for handoff: 
- root cause: rapid autoscaler burst policy + short evaluation window + warmup memory usage on runtime hotpath + intermittent GPU driver resets.
- mitigation applied: burst disabled, minReplicas raised to 8, scale-down cooldown set to 10m, targeted pod resource increases, blocked deploys, progressive node image upgrades planned, ticket RD-INC-4307 created for autoscaler hysteresis.
- outstanding: schedule node driver upgrades (infra), revert deploy-block after stability, postmortem and customer bulletin.

incident-bot: HANDOFF SCHEDULED — carl to hand off to lee-next at 1759006000.

lee: thanks team. I'll stay in monitoring channel. maria keep customer comms ready for postmortem. anya monitor for any residual OOMs and report if counts go above 3 in 10m.

maria: noted. preparing postmortem draft.

carl: handing off in 20. good work everyone. :clap:
